mainEntity.name: How much does a Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A fully rebuilt Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi engine typically costs between £3,000 and £5,000 for supply only, with supply and fit packages ranging from £4,000 to £6,000 depending on the specialist.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of EGR or turbo failure in a Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: The DT224 engine is prone to EGR cooler leaks and turbo actuator wear. Early warning signs include the vehicle entering limp mode, unexplained loss of power under load, white smoke from the exhaust, or coolant loss without visible external leaks.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a classic Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, investing in a rebuilt engine is financially sound for most owners. With classic Land Rover Defender 130 values currently ranging from £15,000 to over £35,000 depending on specification, a replacement preserves the vehicle's value and provides a reliable, warrantied powertrain.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A standard supply and fit service for a Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi typically takes 2 to 3 days at a specialist workshop. This includes removing the old unit, preparing the replacement, installation, and initial running-in checks.

mainEntity.name: Can I upgrade my Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi to a newer L663 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: While engine swaps are popular in the classic Defender community, fitting a modern L663 Ingenium engine requires extensive modifications to the wiring loom, ECU, pedals, and gearbox. EnginesMarket focuses on direct, like-for-like DT224 replacements to ensure seamless compatibility and warranty validity.

historyTimeline.h2: Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: When the 2.2 TDCi (DT224) was introduced to the Defender 130, it replaced the outgoing 2.4 TDCi to meet stricter Euro 5 emissions standards, bringing revised engine management, a new turbocharger, and updated fuel injection while retaining the legendary 8-seat utility of the long-wheelbase chassis.

milestones.description: DT224 (2.2 TDCi), 2.2L, 122hp (Introduced to replace the 2.4 TDCi, featuring a new turbo, revised EGR system, and Euro 5 compliance).
End of classic Defender 130 production, concluding the DT224 era before the transition to the modern L663 Ingenium platform.

commonProblems.h3: The Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi is a robust workhorse, but its emissions equipment and turbocharging introduce specific wear points. The DT224 engine dominates replacement demand for late-model classic Defender 130s, primarily due to EGR cooler leaks and turbo actuator failures. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing these original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.group: EGR Cooler Leaks & Turbo Actuator Wear
problems.h4: EGR Cooler Leaks & Turbo Actuator Wear - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi Loses Power
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler is prone to internal leaks, while the turbo actuator can stick or fail due to heat and carbon buildup, leading to limp mode or loss of power.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace faulty EGR cooler and turbo actuator, clean intake system.
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if the engine block and internals are otherwise healthy.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt DT224 with updated EGR/turbo components, plus 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended for high-mileage units or if secondary damage (e.g., hydrolock from EGR leak) has occurred.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi (2012-2016) currently holds a value of £15,000-£35,000+ in the UK, depending on specification and condition [THIRD-PARTY]. This places it in the £15,000+ band, meaning a £3,000-£5,000 rebuilt engine replacement is a small fraction of the vehicle's worth and is highly recommended to preserve the asset. Flag: Safe.
problems.recommendation: If the engine has high mileage or shows signs of EGR-related coolant loss, a full rebuild is the most reliable long-term solution. A simple EGR/turbo swap on an aged block risks repeat failures.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt DT224 Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi engine prices

problems.h4: Timing Chain Tensioner Wear - Why the Land Rover Defender 130 2.2 TDCi Rattles on Startup
problems.rootCause: The timing chain tensioner can wear over time, leading to chain stretch, rattling noises on startup, and potential catastrophic engine failure if ignored.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace chain, guides, and tensioner as a preventative measure.
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early before internal engine damage occurs.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit of a fully rebuilt DT224 with a new timing chain kit fitted as standard, plus 12-month warranty.
repairOptions.longevity: Best if chain rattle is accompanied by other high-mileage wear or timing-related damage.

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As noted, classic Defender 130 values (£15,000+) easily absorb the cost of a full rebuild, making it a sound investment over repeated minor repairs.
problems.recommendation: For an isolated chain rattle on a low-mileage engine, a specialist chain kit replacement is cost-effective. However, if the engine has high mileage, a rebuilt unit provides a comprehensive, warrantied reset.
